translations.text: 3. Hippolytus of Rome. Chronicle
Adam lived 230 years and begot Seth; Seth lived 205 years and begot Enosh; Enosh lived 190 years and begot Kenan; Kenan lived 170 years and begot Mahalalel.
Mahalalel lived 165 years and begot Jared; Jared lived 162 years and begot Enoch; Enoch lived 165 years and begot Methuselah;
Methuselah lived 187 years and begot Lamech; Lamech lived 188 years and begot Noah; Noah lived 500 years and begot Shem; Shem lived 100 years.
And the Flood was upon the earth for 40 days and 40 nights. In all, the years from Adam to the Flood add up to 2242.
In the second year after the Flood, Shem begot Arphaxad; Arphaxad lived 135 years and begot Salah; Salah lived 130 years and begot Eber;
Eber lived 134 years and begot Peleg; Peleg lived 130 years and begot Reu; Reu lived 135 years and begot Serug;
Serug lived 130 years and begot Nahor; Nahor lived 79 years and begot Terah; Terah lived 70 years and begot Abraham.
Abraham lived 75 years, and God's promise came to him. In all, the years from the Flood to the 75th year of Abraham add up to 1015.
And after God's promise Abraham lived 25 years and begot Isaac; Isaac lived 60 years and begot Jacob;
Jacob lived 87 years and begot Levi; Levi lived 45 years and begot Kohath; Kohath lived 15 years and begot Amram;
Amram lived 70 years and begot Moses; Moses lived 80 years and led the children of Israel out of Egypt into the wilderness.
In all, the years from Abraham's 75th year until the exodus of the children of Israel from Egypt add up to 430 years.
Moses remained with the children of Israel in the wilderness, lived another 40 years, and gave them the Law.
Joshua son of Nun settled them in the land of promise and lived with them 25 years.
In all, the years from the exodus of the children of Israel from Egypt until the division of the land of promise by lot are 65,
and from the time of God's promise to Abraham, 495 years; from the Flood, 1510 years; from Adam, 3672 years.
The judges of Israel: of the elders, 30 years; Chushan-Rishathaim, king of Assyria, 8 years.
Othniel son of Kenaz, 40 years; Eglon king of Moab, 18 years; Ehud, 80 years; Jabin king of Canaan, 20 years;
Deborah and Barak, 40 years; of the Midianites, 7 years; Gideon, 40 years; Abimelech, 3 years; Tola, 20 years; Jair, 22 years;
of the Ammonites, 18 years; Jephthah, 6 years; Ibzan, 7 years; Elon, 10 years; Abdon, 20 years; of the foreigners, 40 years;
Samson, 20 years; Shamgar, 1 year; of the anarchy and the judges Samer [?], 40 years; of the peace [?] and the judges Samania [?], 30 years.
In all, the years of the judges of Israel add up to 520; and those of the priests and judges Eli and Samuel are 90 years. In all, the years of the judges add up to 610 years;
The kings of Judah in Jerusalem: Saul, 30 years. Saul reigned 40 years in all, but for 9 years of his reign Samuel was still judging; David, 35 years and 6 months;
David reigned 40 years in all, but 5 years he reigned during the reign of Saul; and Gad, Nathan, David and Asaph prophesied; Solomon, 40 years.
And he built the temple of God and completed it in the 12th year of his reign;
and Nathan and Ahijah the Shilonite, Shemaiah, and Iddo prophesied. Rehoboam: 18 years; Abijah: 3 years; Asa: 41 years; Jehoshaphat: 25 years;
and Micaiah, Elijah, Elisha, Obadiah, Joel, Oziel, Eleazar, and Azariah prophesied. Jehoram: 8 years; Ahaziah: 1 year; Athaliah, his mother: 7 years;
Joash: 40 years; Amaziah: 29 years; Azariah, who was also called Uzziah, who became a leper: 52 years, and Hosea, Amos, Isaiah, and Jonah prophesied;
Jotham: 16 years; Ahaz: 16 years; Hezekiah: 29 years. In the sixth year of his reign Rome was built by King Romulus;
and in the 10th year of his reign Shalmaneser, king of Assyria, came up against Israel and carried off captive Hoshea, king of Israel, together with the ten tribes.
And in that captivity he carried off Tobit, a righteous man; and in the 14th year of his reign King Hezekiah fell ill.
Isaiah the prophet foretold [?] concerning his death; he wept bitterly. God had mercy and added 15 years to his life.
He gave him a sign through Isaiah the prophet, an 'epanodos' (a going back): the shadow of the sun turned back ten degrees [?].
Manasseh: 55 years; Amon: 2 years; Josiah: 31 years, and Jeremiah, Zephaniah, Huldah, and Baruch prophesied; Jehoahaz: 3 months.
Pharaoh Necho seized Jehoahaz and carried him off captive to Egypt. Jehoiakim, whose name was also Eliakim: 11 years.
Uriah prophesied concerning Jerusalem and fled to Egypt. Jehoiakim sent for him and killed him. Jehoiachin, whose name was Jeconiah: 3 months
and 10 days. Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, seized Jehoiachin, 18 years old, and carried him off captive to Babylon, along with all the mighty men and craftsmen of Jerusalem, some 8,000.
In that captivity he carried off Daniel, Hananiah, Azariah, and Mishael, together with the vessels of the temple and of the city, and he brought that treasure into Babylon;
and he set up as king in Jerusalem, in place of Jehoiachin, Mattaniah, his father's brother, and gave him the name Zedekiah.
All the years from the captivity of Hoshea, king of Israel and of Samaria,
whom Shalmaneser carried off captive, until the carrying off of Jehoiachin, king of Judah, by Nebuchadnezzar, add up to 122 years.
In all, the years of the kings of Judah who reigned
in Jerusalem, from Saul to Jehoiachin, add up to 564 years, and from the exodus of the children of Israel from Egypt, 1,165 years,
and from God's promise to Abraham, 1,595 years; from the Flood, 1,610 years; from Adam, 4,872 years.
The numbers of the years that the children of Israel spent in captivity in Babylon, according to the word of Jeremiah the prophet: Zedekiah: 11 years.
In the second year of Zedekiah, Nebuchadnezzar saw a vision and asked the Chaldeans and the wise men of Babylon about that matter.
God revealed that vision to Daniel, and he made it known to the king. After Zedekiah, Nebuchadnezzar lived as king for 24 years.
Merodach, his son: 12 years; Belshazzar, his brother: 4 years. He made a feast for his nobles and his concubines,
and brought out the vessels that Nebuchadnezzar had taken from Jerusalem, from the house of God, and drank wine from them.
At that time the hand of a man appeared, with its fingers, and it was writing on the wall, and Daniel interpreted this for him.
Darius the Khuzhik [?]: 17 years. In the first year of his reign they threw Daniel into the lions' den.
The king did not want this, but they compelled him because of the decree that had been established. Cyrus the Persian reigned after Darius.
In the first year of Cyrus the seventy years of captivity were fulfilled, in accordance with the word of Jeremiah the prophet.
And King Cyrus sent the children of Israel out of Babylon to Jerusalem with Joshua son of Jozadak, the high priest, and Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel came up with the children of Israel.
Cyrus, king of the Persians, gave back to Jerusalem the vessels of the temple of God, of gold and silver,
which King Nebuchadnezzar had carried away. Daniel and Ezekiel prophesied.
Altogether, the periods from the captivity of Jehoiakim king of Judah to the first year of Cyrus king of the Persians add up to 70 years of captivity;
from Saul, king of Israel, 560 years; from the departure of the children of Israel from Egypt, 1,235 years;
from God's promise to Abraham, 1,665 years; from the Flood, 2,680 years; from Adam, 4,942 years.
Kings of the Persians: Cyrus, after the children of Israel went up to Jerusalem, 30 years;
Cambyses, son of Cyrus, who was called [?] the second Nebuchadnezzar, 9 years. In the fourth year of his reign the Jews rebelled.
He sent the commander Holofernes with a great army to besiege the Jews. Holofernes came with great force and surrounded a city of the Hebrews whose name was Bethulia.
In that city there was a certain woman, a widow, whose name was Judith.
She went down to Holofernes, to his tent, and stayed 3 days. On the fourth day he was sleeping on his bed,
and at night she prayed, and made the help of God her wall, and she cut off his head; and in this way that force of the Persians was scattered.
The Magi: 7 months. Darius son of Hystaspes: 36 years, and in the sixth year of his reign the temple in Jerusalem was completed.
It had been under construction for 46 years. Haggai and Zechariah prophesied.
Xerxes the Great: 19 years and 6 months. In the fourth year of his reign he attacked Egypt, and after that he sawed apart [?] the Athenians.
Artabanus: 7 months. Artaxerxes Longimanus ("Long-Handed"): 41 years.
In the twentieth year of his reign Nehemiah, his cupbearer, asked leave to build Jerusalem, and he was ordered to go up to Judea, and he rebuilt the walls of the city.
He prepared the open space within it, in accordance with the vision of Daniel the prophet; and he learned the Law from Ezra;
and through Esther and Mordecai, Haman was killed in Persia. Xerxes II: 2 months. Sogdianus: 7 months. Darius, the stepson [?], Nothus: 19 years.
Artaxerxes Mnemon: 42 years. Artaxerxes Keuka [?]: 42 years. Arsesoke [Arses?]: 4 years. Darius: 6 years.
Alexander of Macedon killed King Darius and overthrew the power of the Persians. Altogether, the years from Cyrus king of the Persians to King Darius add up to [?] years
230. Alexander, after the killing of Darius, reigned firmly for 26 years and 7 months.
The Ptolemaic kings of the Egyptians: Ptolemy son of Lagus, 42 years.
This Ptolemy gave orders and had those seventy disciples of the Law translate the wisdom of the Jews, the Law and all the books of the Hebrews, into the Greek language;
and in the 18th year of his reign Seleucus Nicator built Antioch.
Ptolemy Philadelphus, 37 years. In the 8th year of his reign Sostratus, Dexiphanes,
the Cnidian, erected at Alexandria the tower called Pharos. In the 21st year of his reign, at Rome, he cut [?] the glory of silver.
Ptolemy Euergetes, 25 years; Ptolemy Philopator, 17 years; Ptolemy Epiphanes, 25 years; Ptolemy Philometor, 11 years;
Ptolemy Euergetes, 23 years; Ptolemy Soter, 27 years; Ptolemy Alexander, 18 years; the second Ptolemy, 18 years;
Ptolemy Dionysus, 19 years; Ptolemy's daughter Cleopatra, 22 years. In all, the years of the Ptolemies of Egypt add up to 294 [?]
259. In the 24th year of the reign of Cleopatra, Julius Caesar came to Rome and the Caesars assembled. And they counted the years by the kings of the Romans.
First, in the 8th year of the reign of Cleopatra, Julius Caesar took [?] from the first men [?]. And Cassius reigned 3 years, 7 months and 10 days.
In the 18th year of the reign of the Romans, 15 [?], Augustus, who reigned at Rome, killed Cleopatra and took the kingdom of the Ptolemies, and after this he reigned another 26 years.
In the 45th year of the reign of the Romans, that is, the 42nd year of the reign of Augustus Caesar, our Savior Jesus Christ became man,
was born and became flesh from the holy Virgin Mary and from the Holy Spirit. In all, the years up to the coming of Christ add up thus:
from the reign of the Ptolemies, the years of Augustus, 26; from Cyrus, who sent the sons of Israel up from Babylon to Jerusalem,
556 years; from Saul, king of Israel, 1116; from the going out of the sons of Israel from Egypt, 1791 years;
and from God's promise to Abraham, 2220 years; from the Flood, 3236; from Adam, 5498 years.
The indiction and the consuls from the 45th year of the reign of the Romans are these. In the 42nd year of Augustus Caesar our Lord Jesus Christ became man.
In the 1st indiction, under the consuls Shabu and Sheterua [?], our Savior and Lord Jesus Christ was born and became flesh from the holy Virgin and Mother of God Mary and from the Holy Spirit.
The indiction goes up to 15 years and then returns again to its beginning.
The Caesars of the Romans. After this his stepson Tiberius became king. In his 18th year was the Passion of the Lord;
Gaius, 4 years; Claudius, 15 years; Nero, 14 years; Galba, Otho and Vitellius, all three, 1 year and 1 month; Vespasian, 10 years;
Titus his son, 3 years; Domitian his brother, 15 years; Nerva, 1 year; Trajan, 20 years; Hadrian the Paralytic, 21 years;
Antoninus Eusebius the Faithful, 22 years; Marcus Aurelius together with Lucius his brother, 19 years; Commodus, 12 years;
Pertinax, 6 months; Severus, 18 years; Antoninus, 7 years; Macrinus, 1 year; Alexander, 19 years.
The mother of this king, Mammaea, was very faithful and a protector of the churches. Maximinus: 3 years; Pupienus and Balbinus: 3 months; Gordian: 6 years; Philip: 7 years.
This one believed in Christ with all his heart. Decius: 9 years, and [?] year[s]; Carinus and his son Numerian: 2 years; Diocletian and Maximian: 29 years.
Maximian, Galerius and Maximus, son of Herculius: 9 years. During the reign of these same men, Constantius, father of the glorious Constantine, reigned over Britain.
The glorious king Constantine, in the 7th year of his reign, killed the lawless king Maximian and took possession of the kingdom of the Romans.
And Constantine the Great died at the age of 65, having spent 32 years in the kingship. In the 19th year of his reign the holy Council of Nicaea took place.
And in the 19th year the holy churches of Jerusalem were consecrated by the hand of holy Athanasius of Alexandria.
Altogether, the years from the coming of Christ to the finding of the Cross come to 326.
From Augustus Caesar to Constantine, 35 kings succeeded one another over the Greeks.
And from James, the brother of the Lord, to Cyril, likewise 35 bishops succeeded one another over Jerusalem.
Constantine, son of the glorious Constantine, and Constans his brother: 3 years; Constantius, their brother, sole ruler: 25 years;
Julian the tormentor of God: 2 years; Jovian: 6 years; Valentinian: 11 years; Enus [?]: 12 days; Valens: 11 years;
Gratian: 11 years; Theodosius the Great: 15 years; Arcadius: 23 years; Honorius: 13 years; Theodosius the Younger: 42 years; Marcian: 6 years; Leo: 20 years;
Leontius: 1 year; Zeno: 16 years; Anastasius: 27 years; Justinian: 29 years; Justin: 9 years; Tiberius: 21 years; Maurice: 14 years;
Phocas: 8 years; Heraclius: 31 years; Constantine and Constantianus: 14 years; Constantine: 28 years; Constantinianus: 22 years;
Leontius: 3 years; Apsimarus: 7 years; Licus [?]: 1 year; Anastasius: 3 years; Theodosius: 1 year; Leo and Constantine his son: 45;
Leo and Constantine and their mother Irene: 26; Nicephorus: 9; Michael: 2; Leo: 8; Michael: 17; Theophilus: 23;
Michael and Theodora his mother: 33; King Basil: 20; Leo, his son, Alexander; Romanus; Constantine; Romanus; Nicephorus Kivrijan [?].
